facts.text: Agriculture comprises 30% of all economic activity in Chilliwack and occupies 65% of the land.
facts.evidence: Agriculture is a predominate industry in Chilliwack that comprises 30% of all economic activity and that occupies 65% of the land.

facts.text: About 2,500 people work in agriculture in Chilliwack, but manufacturing, construction and health care now employ more.
facts.evidence: About 2,500 people work in agriculture, but manufacturing, construction and health care are sectors that now employ more.

facts.text: Canada Education Park in Chilliwack is home to the University of the Fraser Valley, the Justice Institute of BC and the RCMP Pacific Region Training Centre.
facts.evidence: It is home to learning institutions including University of the Fraser Valley, Justice Institute of BC, and RCMP Pacific Region Training Centre.

facts.text: Agriculture is Chilliwack's leading resource sector, and much of the milk and dairy consumed in the Lower Mainland originates there.
facts.evidence: agriculture is the leading resource sector in Chilliwack; much of the milk and dairy products consumed in the lower mainland originates here.

meta.descriptor: a fast-growing Fraser Valley city east of Abbotsford
meta.fact: home to Canada Education Park, with a University of the Fraser Valley campus

overview: Chilliwack counted 93,203 residents in the 2021 Census, up 11.2 percent from 83,788 in 2016, well ahead of the national pace. The median household income was $85,000 in 2020, and the city covers 261.34 square kilometres of suburbs, farms and hillside communities.

Agriculture still drives much of the economy, while manufacturing, construction and health care now employ more people. For a local business, strong growth means new households arriving each year, especially in Sardis and Vedder, alongside a loyal rural customer base.
